messages.author: 563435cd1cb6a261
messages.subject: Linked Statistical Data Analysis
parts:
Hi all,

I'd like to share a Shiny implementation.

I created http://stats.270a.info/

Paper/documentation on the whole thing at:

http://csarven.ca/linked-statistical-data-analysis

Basically the application utilizes federated SPARQL queries to gather
statistical observation values from different endpoints based only on
user's selections (independent, dependent variables, and reference
period). The Shiny application and server bridges the front-end Web user
interface with R on the server-side in order to compare statistical
observations, and stores analysis results in RDF for future research.

Source code at:

https://github.com/csarven/lsd-analysis


So, for instance, here is one analysis that's most likely not that
interesting, but it will give you an idea on how it works:

http://stats.270a.info/analysis/worldbank:SP.DYN.IMRT.IN/transparency:CPI2009/year:2009

Independent variable from World Bank
Dependent variable from Transparency International
Reference period year 2009

There is content negotiation going on for that URI, so if you are using
your Web browser, you'll probably get the .html (regular web UI)
serialization. However, if you requestion for RDF/XML, Turtle, or JSON,
you'll get those serializations e.g.:

curl -LH "Accept: application/rdf+xml"
http://stats.270a.info/analysis/worDYN.IMRT.IN/transparency:CPI2009/year:2009

Since there are way too many combinations, I don't pre-compute and store
them. Instead, I let the users take care of that. Every analysis that's
conducted is written to the RDF store. You can what was analysed so far:

http://stats.270a.info/sparql?query=SELECT+*+WHERE+{+%3Fs+a+%3Chttp%3A%2F%2Fstats.270a.info%2Fvocab%23Analysis%3E+}%0D%0A%0D%0A&default-graph-uri=&output=xml&stylesheet=%2Fxml-to-html-links.xsl



Currently, the application lets you select from the following Linked
Datasets:

* World Bank (only Indicators)
* European Central Bank
* OECD
* FAO of UN
* Transparency International

It can be extended simply by adding more query endpoints.

I plan to add IMF, BIS, and Eurostat soon.

See also: http://270a.info/


I still have *a lot* of things to iron out - I would only call this
version 0.1 - but all feedback is most welcome!

I'll follow up with bite size feedback and questions in separate emails.

And, thanks again to everyone for helping me get through Shiny and
server basics... well, still learning :)

-Sarven
http://csarven.ca/#i
